why: Dogfood cycle 1 (docs/v3/cycles/dogfood-1.md) shows each Issue's title with its reason as the `entity` column's `sub`, as the console's IssueRow shows the reason under or beside the title. At 1800x1200 the sub sits on the title's line, both truncate, and the title of a row with a reason reads `The lo…` or `Pick a…` while the Kind and Origin columns hold empty width (dogfood-1.3, shots `cycle-dogfood--dark--1800x1200.png` and `cycle-dogfood-issue-login-crash--light--1800x1200.png`). The primary column of the table is unreadable for every row that has a sub. `kinds-cells.tsx` draws the sub as a truncating span beside the title, and the entity width is an 18 ch flexible floor.
what: An entity cell never truncates its title to make room for its sub.
owns: unit and layout tests beside them
change: Draw the entity's `sub` under the title (a second line in the cell, muted, truncated on its own) or, if the row height law forbids a second line, give the title the space first: the sub shrinks and hides before the title truncates. Choose by the table's row-height law and say which in the PR. A layout test renders a 60-character title with a 70-character sub in a 1500 px table beside six short columns and asserts the title is not truncated.
proof: make check-fast; the layout test; a shot of /cycle/dogfood at 1800x1200.
acceptance: On /cycle/dogfood at 1800x1200 every title with a reason reads in full where the table has width to spare (shot)
out_of_scope: Column widths of other kinds; the phone card form.
